learningObjective: Precisely define compile-time kernel selection and identify its inputs.
stem: In deep-learning compilers, 'kernel selection' typically refers to which activity?

options.text: Choosing the physical filename of the shared library that will provide the CUDA runtime; this happens at link time and is independent of the model.

Choosing, for each operator instance in the graph, a concrete implementation (library call, generated kernel, or fused template) based on operator type, shape, dtype, layout, and target hardware — with an optional cost model or measurement-based ranking.
Choosing whether to run each iteration of a loop on the CPU or GPU based on runtime input size, decided at every launch by the executor.
Choosing which weights of the model to prune before compilation; kernel selection is another name for structured pruning.

explanation: Kernel selection is the compile-time (or ahead-of-inference) step that maps each op-instance (with its concrete shape, dtype, layout, and target attributes) to a specific implementation from a catalog. Choices commonly include: (i) a hand-tuned library call like cuBLAS/cuDNN, (ii) a generated kernel from Triton/TensorIR/TIR templates, and (iii) a fused template with pointwise epilogues. The selection may be driven by a static cost model, a learned cost model, or by direct measurement. Option B refers to link-time library resolution, unrelated. Option C describes runtime device dispatch. Option D describes pruning, unrelated.

optionExplanations.B: Correct: matches the standard use of the term in TVM, TorchInductor, TensorRT.

assumptions: The compiler operates over a graph where op-instances are already assigned concrete shape/dtype/layout attributes.
A catalog of kernel candidates exists per op-type.
nonImplications: Does not imply kernel selection is trivial; the search space can be very large.
Does not imply the selected kernel is optimal — the cost model may be approximate.

sourceRefs.locator: Kernel selection between ATen, Triton, and CPU C++ templates
